Australia's 2027 Chery Stockman Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Truck Priced From AUD 52,990
12 photos
Photo: Chery
Chinese automaker Chery has released Australian-market pricing information for its plug-in hybrid pickup truck. Gifted with a four-pot diesel, the Stockman is now available in two specifications. AUD 52,990 gets you the lesser grade, whereas the Ultimate will set prospective customers back AUD 57,990 at the very least.
Unique in the segment due to its diesel engine, this fellow competes against the plug-in hybrid gasoline-fueled GWM Cannon and BYD Shark 6. Its 2.5-liter turbo diesel plug-in hybrid setup is listed up to 350 kilowatts (469 horsepower) and 800 Newton-meters (590 pound-feet) of twist, numbers that should appeal to a plethora of buyers.
Priced below the BYD yet pricier than the GWM, the Chery produces a respectable 140 kW (188 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) without any kind of electrified assistance. A four-speed hybrid tranny handles power delivery, whereas a 34-kWh battery of the lithium-iron-phosphate variety enables full-electric driving.
Chery advertises up to 100 kilometers (62 miles) of electric-only range on the NEDC test cycle, which is curious when you remember that NEDC is very old news. The high-voltage battery supports DC fast charging at up to 70 kilowatts and AC charging at no more than 6.6 kilowatts.
In addition to the under-tub LFP battery, customers also get an 80-liter fuel tank. On the combined test cycle, it should consume anything between 1.0 and 1.1 liters of diesel per 100 kilometers while emitting 25 to 30 grams of CO2 per kilometer. All in all, not bad at all. Both grades of the diesel-fueled Stockman employ four-wheel drive.
Photo: Chery Center and rear diff locks are standard on the base Urban spec. Equipped with leaf springs out back and double wishbones for the front axle, the Stockman rides on 18-inch wheels and provides up to 235 millimeters (9.3 inches) of ground clearance. A dual cab that measures 3,250 millimeters (128 inches) between its axles, the Chinese newcomer is up there with the segment's bests in terms of towing capacity.
Chery advertises 3,495 kilograms (7,705 pounds) braked and 750 kilograms (1,653 pounds) unbraked. The maximum payload rating of 810 kilograms (1,786 pounds) only applies to the Urban trim level. Opting for the Ultimate gets you more standard kit, including a front differential lock, 14 audio speakers, and a head-up display.
AUD 5,000 pricier, the Ultimate further sweetens the deal with a digital rearview mirror, a heated steering wheel, plus heating and ventilation for the front seats. In the Australian market, customer deliveries are scheduled to start in February 2027. That gives Aussie buyers a few short months to decide whether the diesel-electric combo makes more sense than current gasoline-electric alternatives or a purely diesel pickup.
Going forward, Chery 's Australian subsidiary plans to introduce a gasoline plug-in hybrid. Due in the second half of 2027, presumably as a 2028 model, the second powertrain is estimated to generate a frankly ridiculous 395 kilowatts (530 horsepower) and 1,000 Newton-meters (738 pound-feet).
